ActionOutcome.description:
One attempted action and what the world did about it.

`outcome_id` is runtime-owned. A planner may cite it as evidence for a
later memory, which is only sound because the planner cannot mint one: an
outcome exists after its action has already been assessed, so a plan
physically cannot cite the success of its own future steps.
ActionOutcome.title: ActionOutcome

ActionOutcomeDigest.description: Compact immutable evidence retained for the lifetime of one run.
ActionOutcomeDigest.title: ActionOutcomeDigest

ActiveFieldbookProject.description: The one explicitly selected project allowed a fuller automatic summary.
ActiveFieldbookProject.title: ActiveFieldbookProject

AdvertisedTask.description:
One task Kenshi confirms the current selection may issue to a target.

The value and name are the game's own; mapping either onto a controller
semantic is the operation registry's job, not this model's. `source` records
that the context-menu builder vouched for it; other sources fail strict
validation instead of becoming compatibility affordances.
AdvertisedTask.title: AdvertisedTask

AdvertisedTaskSource.description:
How Kenshi was asked.

The only accepted authority is the context-menu builder. Keeping the source
explicit prevents a future proxy from entering the wire unnoticed.
AdvertisedTaskSource.title: AdvertisedTaskSource

AdvisorBriefEvidence.description: Advice, not world evidence. Rendered as such wherever it is stored.
AdvisorBriefEvidence.title: AdvisorBriefEvidence

ApproachDialogueTargetAction.description:
Initiate dialogue with one exact currently observed dialogue target.

Reusable and target-generic: the target is any current non-hostile person
the telemetry already reports as talkable, vendor or not. The action names
only a stable observed identity, never a role, a scenario, or a coordinate.
The controller issues Kenshi's native talk-to order and owns the whole
monitored interaction, so there is no planner-visible "continue
approaching" or prerequisite unpause command.
ApproachDialogueTargetAction.title: ApproachDialogueTargetAction

CanonicalCompactionProvenance.description: Exact immutable candidate and application identity behind a replacement.
CanonicalCompactionProvenance.title: CanonicalCompactionProvenance

CanonicalFieldbookProvenance.description: Exact planner context and resolved sources behind a fieldbook change.
CanonicalFieldbookProvenance.title: CanonicalFieldbookProvenance

CanonicalMemoryProvenance.description: The exact accepted lifecycle operation and the authority behind it.
CanonicalMemoryProvenance.title: CanonicalMemoryProvenance

CharacterWorkState.description:
Independent retained-work channels and current activity.

Kenshi's ordinary order queue, configured Jobs, permanent Jobs, and current
goal have separate owners and lifetimes. None is inferred from another.
The controller-issued command remains separate in ``controller_commands``.
CharacterWorkState.title: CharacterWorkState

CloseActiveInterfaceAction.description:
Return from the currently blocking interface to the world.

The action deliberately names no widget, caption, or coordinate. Native
code closes the interface families the controller can cause or observe and
acknowledges success only after Kenshi reports no remaining dialogue,
message box, Prospecting window, inventory pair, or ordinary GUI window.
CloseActiveInterfaceAction.title: CloseActiveInterfaceAction

CompactionMethod.description:
Implemented compaction treatments.

Semantic rewriting is deliberately absent until it can satisfy the same
source-conservation and atomic-application contract as the lossless path.
CompactionMethod.title: CompactionMethod

ConsultAdvisorAction.description:
Ask a read-only guide-grounded model for strategic advice.

This is a cognitive action. It emits no controller primitives, never enters
the environment dispatch path, and cannot directly change Kenshi state.
ConsultAdvisorAction.title: ConsultAdvisorAction

ContextMenuProbe.description: What the native sampler could prove about Kenshi's context menu.
ContextMenuProbe.title: ContextMenuProbe

ContinuityReceiptDigest.description: Bounded planner feedback for one full continuity operation receipt.
ContinuityReceiptDigest.title: ContinuityReceiptDigest

CurrentObservationEvidence.description: The exact observation the planner was looking at when it wrote this.
CurrentObservationEvidence.title: CurrentObservationEvidence

DiscoveredObject.description:
One nearby object and what Kenshi says it can be ordered to do.

Reconnaissance, not a routed affordance. `world_targets` is the surface the
controller has semantic routes for; this is the surface that exists. The
gap between them is the implementation queue, and it is derived from the
game rather than from anyone noticing an absence.

Presence here authorizes nothing. A task appearing means Kenshi answered
yes to "may this selection order this object to do that", which is a fact
about the game, not permission for the controller to try it.
DiscoveredObject.title: DiscoveredObject

EvidenceAuthority.description: What one resolved identity is actually capable of establishing.
EvidenceAuthority.title: EvidenceAuthority

ExitCurrentBuildingAction.description:
Leave the selected character's current building through a native door.

The planner supplies no coordinates, bearing, door identity, or retry
strategy. The native controller resolves an unlocked door from the exact
building the selected character currently occupies, issues one pathing
order to its outdoor point, and owns completion or typed failure.
ExitCurrentBuildingAction.title: ExitCurrentBuildingAction

FieldbookProjectIndex.description: Bounded metadata automatically shown without full project entries.
FieldbookProjectIndex.title: FieldbookProjectIndex

GroundPosition.description:
A position on Kenshi's ground plane.

Kenshi's world is x/z at ground level with y as altitude, so a
two-component ground position is x and z. `Vec2` is a screen-space x/y and
means something different; reusing it here would have quietly relabelled an
axis.
GroundPosition.title: GroundPosition

InventorySectionView.description: One named grid within an inventory.
InventorySectionView.title: InventorySectionView

InventorySlotItem.description:
One item in one inventory slot, with the coordinates that name it.

`x`/`y` are not decoration. Kenshi's own transfer takes a section name and a
slot, so the slot *is* the item's address to the engine - unlike a cell
label scraped off a MyGUI widget, which addresses a picture of it.
InventorySlotItem.title: InventorySlotItem

KeepMemoryOperation.description:
Create one durable record from something already established.

`evidence` is absent on purpose. The stored grounding string is rendered by
the runtime from `references` after each one resolves, so a record can
never describe proof it does not have.
KeepMemoryOperation.title: KeepMemoryOperation

KnownMapDestination.description:
A settlement marker the current player has actually discovered.

The stable identity and player-visible name authorize a semantic journey.
The controller owns the exact waypoint; no world coordinate is exposed to
or authored by the planner.
KnownMapDestination.title: KnownMapDestination

MemoryAuthorship.description:
Who stands behind a record, and how much that is worth.

`legacy_unverified` marks rows written before continuity had grounding at
all. They are kept because they are real user data, not because anything
checked them.
MemoryAuthorship.title: MemoryAuthorship

MemoryCompactionCandidate.description: A bounded proposal that has no authority until atomically applied.
MemoryCompactionCandidate.title: MemoryCompactionCandidate

MemoryCompactionGenerator.description: How one candidate was produced, including honest non-use of a prompt.
MemoryCompactionGenerator.title: MemoryCompactionGenerator

MemoryReadReceipt.description: Runtime identity and provenance for one planner-requested memory read.
MemoryReadReceipt.title: MemoryReadReceipt

MemoryRecord.description: One durable record, projected from its lifecycle history.
MemoryRecord.title: MemoryRecord

MemoryResolutionDisposition.description: What resolving an intention or uncertainty actually concluded.
MemoryResolutionDisposition.title: MemoryResolutionDisposition

MemoryStatus.description: Where a record sits in its lifecycle. Only `active` reaches recall.
MemoryStatus.title: MemoryStatus

MoveInDirectionAction.description:
Walk a bearing and a distance from wherever the character is standing.

The intended destination is a point, not a person, so this action models
movement even when no nearby character can serve as a destination. Its
native request and acknowledgement deliberately carry an empty target ID;
command identity is the keyed command, selected character, bearing, and
distance.

`bearing_degrees` is clockwise from north, as read on the map: 0 north,
90 east, 180 south, 270 west.
MoveInDirectionAction.title: MoveInDirectionAction

MoveToCharacterAction.description:
Walk to any exact observed nearby character without talking to them.

Movement used to be possible only toward someone the agent could hold a
conversation with, so inside a building holding two people that was the
whole reachable world: it sold what it could, asked both for work, recorded
that it was repeating itself, and had no action that could take it
anywhere. Nearby characters are reported within four hundred units, which
across a town is most of it, so walking to a person is how the agent gets
to a place - the destination is a stable observed identity, never a
coordinate.
MoveToCharacterAction.title: MoveToCharacterAction

OpenInventory.description:
One inventory Kenshi currently has open, whatever owns it.

Read from `ForgottenGUI::inventoryWindowsOpen`, the engine's own map of
owner handle to window, which holds no opinion about what kind of thing the
owner is. The field it replaces read one of four typed slots and saw only
buildings, so a looted body's window had no exported owner at all: the agent
ordered looting, Kenshi opened the window, and nothing told the agent an
inventory was there or what was in it.

A body, a crate, a shop and a squadmate all arrive here the same way, which
is what lets one transfer serve looting, buying, giving and harvesting
without knowing which it is looking at.
OpenInventory.title: OpenInventory

OpenTradeWindowAction.description:
Put two inventories side by side, in Kenshi's own terms.

`showInventory` opens one window - a character's personal gear, the view a
player gets for stealing - so a transfer opened that way has nothing to move
between. `ForgottenGUI::showTradeWindow` takes both sides and a type, and
that type enum is the engine stating that trading and looting are one
mechanism with a flag rather than two problems.
OpenTradeWindowAction.title: OpenTradeWindowAction

PerformCharacterOrderAction.description:
Issue one order Kenshi already says this person affords.

Deliberately one operation rather than a verb per gameplay action. The
plug-in asks Kenshi to build the exact context menu it would show for the
target while muting only the renderer. Which orders apply to a bandit, a
corpse, or a downed squadmate is therefore the engine's judgment, arriving
in telemetry as `advertised_tasks`. Attacking, looting, and first aid are
then the same operation with a different name on it.

The alternative -- one typed action per verb, each with its own eligibility
fence -- means re-deriving in Python what the game already computed, and
getting a new disposition gate wrong once per verb.

`order` is the advertised task name, lowercased. The exact string that
arrived in telemetry is the one that goes back out, so a command stays
legible in a run bundle without a lookup table.
PerformCharacterOrderAction.title: PerformCharacterOrderAction

PerformContextAction.description:
Perform one exact contextual task an observed world object advertises.

The planner copies only a `(target_id, context_action)` pair from current
`context_targets`. Native code re-resolves the object, rechecks the reviewed
task, issues Kenshi's own default order, and proves the selected character's
AI accepted that exact object/task pair.
PerformContextAction.title: PerformContextAction

PlanOutcome.description:
Why a plan ended, in terms of what it originally set out to do.

Without this the next planner reconstructs purpose from "Execute step X",
which is not a purpose. The objective is copied from the plan that carried
it, and the reason is the executor's terminal verdict — neither is written
by a model after the fact.
PlanOutcome.title: PlanOutcome

PlanOutcomeDigest.description: Compact immutable plan lifecycle retained for the lifetime of one run.
PlanOutcomeDigest.title: PlanOutcomeDigest

PlatoonState.description: One player platoon and its exact observed roster membership.
PlatoonState.title: PlatoonState

ProduceResourceOutputAction.description: Internal production phase retained until a bounded output yield exists.
ProduceResourceOutputAction.title: ProduceResourceOutputAction

ProspectReading.description:
One line as Kenshi's Prospecting window displays it.

The label is verbatim. The window builds each line from a resource name and
a value but exposes only the button, so the exact split is unproven -
parsing it here would assert a format nobody has confirmed. Whatever
structure this turns out to have can be modelled once it is observed.
ProspectReading.title: ProspectReading

ProspectSurvey.description:
One completed prospecting survey, tied to the command that asked for it.

Read from the game's own window rather than the terrain field beneath it,
so the agent sees what a player would see. Deliberately a pulse: it knows
what it surveyed and where it stood, not what exists everywhere.

The readings are area coverage, not deposit counts. A discrete iron node
occupies a trivial fraction of the surveyed area, so it can read near zero
while the deposit is plainly there - which is why this is not the channel
for finding deposits. `world_targets` already carries those by coordinate
with quality levels; this is the wider picture around them.
ProspectSurvey.title: ProspectSurvey

ReadFieldbookAction.description: Electively inspect bounded private project context without game input.
ReadFieldbookAction.title: ReadFieldbookAction

RecallMemoryAction.description:
Deliberately read continuity beyond what automatic context already showed.

A cognitive action. It emits no controller primitives, never enters the
environment dispatch path, spends no pointer, purchase, or native risk
budget, and cannot authorize anything. Durable memory searches active
records; working-outcome searches resurface compact runtime-owned evidence
that scrolled out of the rich recent window.
RecallMemoryAction.title: RecallMemoryAction

RecallSummary.description:
What automatic recall left out, stated rather than implied.

A planner that cannot tell "nothing else exists" from "more exists, not
shown" will conclude the first and stop looking.
RecallSummary.title: RecallSummary

RecallTier.description:
Why a record was chosen, in the order the tiers are spent.

The order is the policy: a plan cannot safely proceed without its open
commitments or what it knows about the entity in front of it, so those are
not allowed to compete with general knowledge for the same slots.
RecallTier.title: RecallTier

RegroupWithSquadMemberAction.description: Bring the selected actor to one exact current squadmate.
RegroupWithSquadMemberAction.title: RegroupWithSquadMemberAction

ReinforceMemoryOperation.description: Say an existing record still matters, without writing a second copy.
ReinforceMemoryOperation.title: ReinforceMemoryOperation

ResolveMemoryOperation.description: Close an open commitment or question with the evidence that closed it.
ResolveMemoryOperation.title: ResolveMemoryOperation

ResolvedEvidenceSnapshot.description: Typed immutable truth retained after a reference leaves planner context.
ResolvedEvidenceSnapshot.title: ResolvedEvidenceSnapshot

ResourceOutputItem.description: One exact item stack in a natural resource's engine-owned output slot.
ResourceOutputItem.title: ResourceOutputItem

RespondToImmediateThreatAction.description:
Choose whether one selected actor engages or withdraws from a threat.

The runtime owns playback, an observed escape vector for withdrawal,
continuous threat and squad-health observation, timeout, interruption, and
the terminal pause. The planner chooses only the actor and gameplay policy.
RespondToImmediateThreatAction.title: RespondToImmediateThreatAction

RetractMemoryOperation.description: Withdraw a record from active recall without deleting its history.
RetractMemoryOperation.title: RetractMemoryOperation

RuntimeContextMenu.description:
Exact game-owned menu orders, distinct from reviewed action authority.

``task_type_values`` deliberately retains numeric values that the pinned
TaskType vocabulary does not yet name. Observing a menu item must never
make it executable; only ``WorldTarget.context_actions`` carries that
separately reviewed authority.
RuntimeContextMenu.title: RuntimeContextMenu

SelectSquadMemberExactAction.description: Select one exact squad member through native stable identity.
SelectSquadMemberExactAction.title: SelectSquadMemberExactAction

SetSpeedAction.description:
Set a running playback state at one of Kenshi's three ordinal gears.

This is one semantic transition even when Kenshi is paused. The controller
owns starting at gear 1 before selecting a faster gear, because the faster
keys do not themselves resume a paused world.
SetSpeedAction.title: SetSpeedAction

ShiftIntoBodyAction.description:
Become one exact currently observed character.

Control in Kenshi follows selection rather than roster membership - a
character released from the active platoon keeps taking orders while absent
from the squad menu - so entering a body means belonging to the player
faction and being the selected primary. The body is placed in its own squad:
inhabiting someone is not gaining a follower, and the bodies left behind
stay their own unit rather than accumulating into a retinue of former hosts.

This is the operation that makes a total party loss survivable. It is not
restricted to that case, because an agent that can only change bodies while
dying cannot practise the thing it will need to do while dying.
ShiftIntoBodyAction.title: ShiftIntoBodyAction

StateChange.description:
One field of the world that moved since the previous observation.

Deliberately carries the values and not just the path. "money changed" does
not tell an agent whether its purchase went through; "money 118 -> 96" does,
and that is the difference between noticing a failed action and repeating it.
StateChange.title: StateChange

StopAction.description:
End the whole run, not the current plan.

The distinction is not obvious from the name and was undocumented, so a
planner that had finished what it set out to do used this to say "that
objective is complete" and ended an eighty-step run on step eleven, with a
reason that read "resuming free play to pursue next objective". A plan ends
by its steps completing; this ends the agent.
StopAction.title: StopAction

SupersedeMemoryOperation.description: Replace a record and link the old one to its replacement, atomically.
SupersedeMemoryOperation.title: SupersedeMemoryOperation

SurveyLocalResourcesAction.description:
Survey Kenshi's resource field where the selected character stands.

The prospecting reading the game's own window is built from, returned as a
grid rather than the single averaged number that window displays. That
average is why a zone can report `Iron: 0` while two iron deposits sit in
it: a discrete node covers a trivial fraction of the surveyed area. A grid
keeps direction and distance.

The planner supplies nothing. Where the character stands is the survey,
which is what makes this an action with a cost rather than free perception.
SurveyLocalResourcesAction.title: SurveyLocalResourcesAction

TaskCollection.description: One bounded task container without a fabricated total.
TaskCollection.title: TaskCollection

TaskCollectionCompleteness.description: Whether absence from one bounded Kenshi task channel is meaningful.
TaskCollectionCompleteness.title: TaskCollectionCompleteness

TaskEntry.description:
One entry read from one exact Kenshi task channel.

Nullable facts are required on the wire. ``None`` means the source did not
prove the value; an empty string or an array position is never substituted
for an unknown target or queue position.
TaskEntry.title: TaskEntry

ToolTipLine.description:
One tooltip row as the game stores it: a label and its value.

Kenshi's `ToolTipLine` keeps the two in separate boxes - "Value" / "c.5,165"
- so a price is a lookup rather than a parse.
ToolTipLine.title: ToolTipLine

TransferItemAction.description:
Move one item between two open inventories, whatever owns them.

Looting a body, buying from a shop, handing something to a squadmate and
emptying a mining crate are one model-level move with different owners.
The plug-in removes the item from the source `Inventory` and tries to add it
to the destination. When a shop trade is open, the project applies a
deliberately simplified price from `Item::getValueSingle`; it does not call
`InventoryGUI::RClickAutoTrade` or inherit Kenshi's theft, faction-standing,
stolen-goods, or haggling adjudication.

The slot is the address. `InventorySection::getItemAt(x, y)` resolves the
source item, so `(section_name, slot_x, slot_y)` names it to the model,
unlike a cell label read off a widget, which names a picture of it.
TransferItemAction.title: TransferItemAction

TravelToMapDestinationAction.description:
Travel to one exact settlement marker already known to the player.

Native code re-resolves the discovered marker, chooses Kenshi's waypoint,
issues one pathing order, and owns camera follow and arrival. The planner
never supplies map coordinates or re-authors movement pulses.
TravelToMapDestinationAction.title: TravelToMapDestinationAction

WorldTarget.description:
A non-character object with exact reviewed contextual affordances.

This is the semantic equivalent of what a player learns by right-clicking
an object. A listed action authorizes an exact bounded attempt, not a
prediction that Kenshi will accept or complete it. The native controller
proves acceptance causally from the selected character's exact AI goal.
Absence means unsupported, never permission to improvise a click.
WorldTarget.title: WorldTarget
